stem: What metric does the Routing Information Protocol (RIP) use?

options.content: The number of hops
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The bandwidth of the link
options.rationale: Bandwidth-based cost is used by OSPF.

options.content: The length of the cable in metres
options.rationale: RIP does not measure the length of a cable.

options.content: The number of users on the network
options.rationale: The number of users is not a routing metric.

explanation: RIP counts routers (hops).

stem: What is the largest number of hops that RIP allows for a reachable route?

options.rationale: Correct: 16 means unreachable.
The limit is higher than 8.
A route of 16 hops is treated as unreachable.
The limit is much smaller than 255.

explanation: RIP allows at most 15 hops.

stem: What type of protocol is OSPF?

options.content: Distance-vector
options.rationale: That is RIP.

options.content: Static
options.rationale: Static routes are set by hand, not by a protocol.

options.content: Application-layer
options.rationale: OSPF is a routing protocol, not an application protocol such as HTTP.

options.content: Link-state
options.rationale: Correct: each router has a map of the network.

explanation: OSPF is link-state.

stem: What is meant by dynamic routing?

options.content: An administrator types every route into each router by hand each time
options.rationale: That describes static routing.

options.content: Packets always take the same route
options.rationale: Dynamic routing allows the route to change.

options.content: Routers learn and update routes automatically using a protocol
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Routers do not use routing tables
options.rationale: All routers use routing tables.

explanation: Routers exchange information so that the tables change when the network changes.

stem: Which is a weakness of RIP?

options.content: It needs all the routers to build a full map of the whole network
options.rationale: That is how OSPF works.

options.content: It sends an update only when a link fails
options.rationale: RIP also sends its table at regular intervals.

options.content: It uses areas to divide large networks
options.rationale: Areas belong to OSPF.

options.content: It ignores the speed of the links when choosing a route
options.rationale: Correct: it counts hops only.

explanation: A short route over slow links can be chosen.

stem: In OSPF what is stored in the link-state database?

options.content: The web pages recently visited by users
options.rationale: Routers do not store web pages in the database.

options.content: Only the hop count from the router to each of its direct neighbours
options.rationale: Hop count is the RIP metric.

options.content: The state and cost of the links of all the routers in the area
options.rationale: Correct: it gives each router a map.

options.content: The user names and passwords
options.rationale: Routing databases do not hold passwords of users.

explanation: Every router in the area holds the same map.
hints: What does each router need to build a map?

stem: A company in Mutare has 40 routers in five towns, with links ranging from 1 Mbit/s to 1 Gbit/s, and some routes of more than 15 hops. Which protocol is the better choice?

options.content: RIP, because it is simple to set up and has no limit on the size of the network or the hops
options.rationale: RIP has a limit of 15 hops.

options.content: OSPF, because it uses link costs, adjusts quickly and divides the network into areas
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: RIP, because it chooses the fastest links
options.rationale: RIP counts hops and ignores link speed.

options.content: Static routing only, because routes never change
options.rationale: Links fail and change; static routes would not adjust.

explanation: Large networks with mixed link speeds need link-state routing.
hints: Compare the number of hops with the limit of RIP.

stem: OSPF chooses the route with the lowest total cost.
explanation: True. Cost is based on link bandwidth and the costs along the route are added.

stem: In RIP each router builds a map of the whole network.
explanation: False. RIP routers only know what their neighbours tell them. Building a map is what OSPF routers do.

stem: Match each feature to RIP or OSPF.

left.content: Sends its whole table every 30 seconds

explanation: RIP: distance-vector, 15 hops, whole table. OSPF: link-state, cost.

stem: Complete the sentences about routing.

payload.template: Routes typed in by an administrator are called {{blank:a}} routes. RIP uses the {{blank:b}} count as its metric. OSPF uses the idea of {{blank:c}} algorithm to find the shortest path.

explanation: Static, hop, Dijkstra's.
hints: OSPF computes shortest paths on a map.

stem: An OSPF router uses the rule cost = 100 ÷ bandwidth in Mbit/s. What is the cost of a 20 Mbit/s link?

A network has these links, with OSPF costs.

| Link | OSPF cost |
|:-:|:-:|
| P - Q | 20 |
| Q - T | 20 |
| P - R | 5 |
| R - S | 5 |
| S - T | 5 |
| T - U | 10 |

RIP chooses the route with the fewest hops from P to U. How many hops does it use?
explanation: P-Q-T-U has 3 hops.
workedSolution:
1. The routes are P-Q-T-U (3 hops) and P-R-S-T-U (4 hops).
2. RIP chooses P-Q-T-U: 3 hops.
hints: Count the routers or links between P and U for the shortest number of hops.

stem:
Use the network below.

| Link | OSPF cost |
|:-:|:-:|
| P - Q | 20 |
| Q - T | 20 |
| P - R | 5 |
| R - S | 5 |
| S - T | 5 |
| T - U | 10 |

Calculate the total cost of the route that OSPF chooses from P to U.
explanation: The route via R and S costs 25, less than 50.
workedSolution:
1. P-Q-T-U costs 20 + 20 + 10 = 50.
2. P-R-S-T-U costs 5 + 5 + 5 + 10 = 25.
3. OSPF chooses the lower cost: 25.
hints: Add the costs of the links on each route.

stem:
The network has these links.

| Link | OSPF cost |
|:-:|:-:|
| P - Q | 20 |
| Q - T | 20 |
| P - R | 5 |
| R - S | 5 |
| S - T | 5 |
| T - U | 10 |

Which statement about the routes from P to U is correct?

options.content: RIP and OSPF choose the same route
options.rationale: RIP prefers the route with fewer hops, which is not the cheapest route.

options.content: RIP and OSPF choose different routes
options.rationale: Correct: RIP uses P-Q-T-U, OSPF uses P-R-S-T-U.

options.content: Both choose P-R-S-T-U because it has fewer hops
options.rationale: P-R-S-T-U has more hops than P-Q-T-U.

options.content: Both choose P-Q-T-U because its links are faster
options.rationale: Its links have the higher costs, so they are slower.

explanation: RIP chooses the 3-hop route, OSPF chooses the 25-cost route.
hints: Compare the hop count and the cost of each route.

stem: Describe how a router using RIP learns routes. [4]

points.description: Each router sends its routing table to its neighbours at regular intervals (every 30 seconds)
A router receiving a table adds 1 to the hop count of each route
It keeps the route with the fewest hops to each network
A route of 16 hops is treated as unreachable

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each router sends its routing table to its neighbours every 30 seconds. A receiving router adds 1 to the hop count of each route and keeps the route with the fewest hops to each network. A route of 16 hops is treated as unreachable.

explanation: Regular tables, add one hop, keep the best, 16 is unreachable.
hints: Two differences in how they work.

stem: Describe how a router using OSPF decides on the best route to a network. [4]

points.description: Each router tells the other routers in its area the state and cost of its links
Each router stores this in its link-state database, giving it a map of the network
The router calculates the lowest-cost path to each network using a shortest-path (Dijkstra) algorithm
It puts the next hop of the lowest-cost path in its routing table

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each router tells the other routers in its area the state and cost of its links. Each router stores this in its link-state database, which gives it a map of the network. It then calculates the lowest-cost path to each network with a shortest-path algorithm and puts the next hop in its routing table.

explanation: Advertise, database, calculate, table.

stem: Give three reasons why OSPF is better than RIP for a large network. [3]

points.description: It is not limited to 15 hops and the network can be divided into areas
It uses a cost based on the speed of the links so it chooses faster routes
It adjusts quickly to a change because only changes are sent to all the routers in the area

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It has no 15-hop limit and the network can be divided into areas. It uses a cost based on link speed so it chooses faster routes, and it adjusts quickly because changes are sent at once to all routers in the area.

explanation: Size, cost metric, speed of adjusting.
hints: Think about size, adjusting after a failure and link speed.

stem: State two disadvantages of static routing in a large network. [2]

points.description: Every route must be entered and changed by hand, which takes a lot of work
If a link fails the routes are not updated and packets are lost until the administrator corrects them

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Every route has to be entered and changed by hand, and if a link fails the routes are not updated, so packets are lost until the administrator corrects them.

explanation: Manual work and no automatic repair.
hints: What happens when a link fails?

| Link | OSPF cost |
|:-:|:-:|
| P - Q | 20 |
| Q - T | 20 |
| P - R | 5 |
| R - S | 5 |
| S - T | 5 |
| T - U | 10 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the number of hops on the route P-Q-T-U.
parts.workedSolution:
1. The links are P-Q, Q-T and T-U.
2. That is 3 hops.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the OSPF cost of the route P-Q-T-U.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the OSPF cost of the route P-R-S-T-U.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State the route chosen by RIP and the route chosen by OSPF, and explain why they are different.

points.description: RIP chooses P-Q-T-U because it has the fewest hops (3)
OSPF chooses P-R-S-T-U because its total cost (25) is lower than 50

hints: Add the costs for OSPF; count the links for RIP.

stem: A school group in Masvingo has a campus network with 5 routers, all within 3 hops of each other, managed by one part-time technician. A hospital group has a network of 90 routers over many towns, with routes of up to 20 hops and links of different speeds.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Recommend a routing protocol for the school and give one reason.

points.description: RIP
It is simple to set up and the network is well within the 15-hop limit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: RIP, because it is simple to set up and the network is well within the 15-hop limit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why RIP is unsuitable for the hospital network.

points.description: Routes of 20 hops are more than the maximum of 15 hops, so those routers would be unreachable
RIP ignores the speed of the links and adjusts slowly in a big network

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Routes of 20 hops are more than RIP's maximum of 15, so some routers would be unreachable, and RIP ignores link speed and adjusts slowly in a large network.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe two features of OSPF that suit the hospital network.

points.description: The network can be divided into areas, so databases and calculations stay small
The cost is based on link speed and updates are sent only when something changes

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The network can be divided into areas to keep each database small, and the cost is based on link speed with updates sent only when something changes.

explanation: A single campus with a few routers suits RIP; a large national network needs OSPF.
hints: Link each answer to the numbers in the scenario.
